validation.notes: Repaired packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts: recoverToolInvocation now takes the durable cancellation into account (guard is `!cancelled && call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe"`). Previously a restored effect_pending call whose call policy and tool policy were both "safe" cleared its replay checkpoint via clearReplayCheckpoint and re-ran the tool even when the run control was already cancel_requested in the parallel driver path, so a newly interrupted batch replayed after cancellation. With the guard, cancelled recovery leaves the durable checkpoint intact, performs no tool invocation, and publishes interruptedOutcome (durable checkpoint content + the 'external outcome is unknown' interruption marker, isError true, terminate false) through publishToolOutcome; non-cancelled safe/safe recovery still clears the checkpoint, replays exactly once with the persisted arguments and settles through a single outcome publication. .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real module and real recoverToolInvocation/interruptedOutcome via .prale-eval/subject.mjs (createRecoverySubject) and asserts observable boundary events and published outcomes across 8 scenarios: cancelled safe/safe (event order exactly [read, publish], no clear/invoke, zero effects, checkpoint content + details preserved), cancelled with absent/never/plain-replay tools, cancelled with a non-safe call, cancelled with an empty checkpoint (marker only, no invented details), non-cancelled safe/safe (event order [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish], exactly one effect, result published with checkpoint-cleared arguments and recovery marking) and non-cancelled non-safe combinations still publishing interrupted evidence. Verified by temporarily reverting the one-line guard: the script then fails with AssertionError ('cancelled batch must only read the checkpoint and publish, got clear,invoke,effect-complete,publish' etc.) and exits non-zero, then passes again (exit 0) with the guard restored. The workspace has no node_modules, so the repository's own vitest suites (packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-tools.test.ts) could not be executed here; validation relies on the standalone Node 24 VM-module/subject harness, which needed no dependencies or network. No other production call site clears replay checkpoints (clearReplayCheckpoint has a single caller), and no TASK.md, subject.mjs, lockfile, git or harness files were modified.
